title: A belief and a discovery
lines: Newton’s religious convictions belong to history; what makes his discoveries reliable is another question.
Between Faith and Evidence asks how a thinker's private beliefs relate to claims everyone can examine.
The book responds to arguments that place famous scientists neatly on a religious or secular side.

title: Lives beyond the camps
lines: Their actual lives are more complicated, and often more interesting, than those competing lists suggest.
Through historical lives, it separates personal belief, public evidence, and the meaning people find in discovery.
It also asks what classrooms should preserve when intellectual history and scientific explanation meet.
